Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the wanted utilisation, the overtime rule, the employer extra, the late rent limit, the wanted pay share and the retail target.
Check Team, Services and Resources. They hold the owner, the technicians, the front desk, the outside contacts, the 20 services and the four chairs and the treatment room.
Use Pay Runs every month: type the takings, tips, hours and the booth rent. Total cost to the studio, days late and the pay check fill in by themselves.
Keep Commission Statements and Hourly Timesheets for the technician on commission and the hourly team. Overtime and gross pay follow the rule in Start.
Record every booth rent in Booth Rent Ledger: a booth renter is a technician who rents a chair and keeps their own takings. Late rent shows as arrears and goes to Rent Chase Log.
Use Tips Ledger to pass on card tips after the card fee and to see what is still owed to each technician.
Fill Technician Months and Technician Days. Utilisation (the share of bookable minutes that are sold), revenue per booked hour and the overload flag calculate themselves.
Set the wanted figures for each technician in Productivity Targets, then read Service Mix, Reviews and Retail by Technician to see who needs help and what to coach.
Plan Schedules and Time Off, record Training Log courses and write each Check-in with the next step and the review date.

Use the 14 calculators to test a commission, overtime, rent income, a late rent step, a pay model and a new technician. Employment and tax rules stay generic: check your own local rules or an adviser.
Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in. Read the Technician Dashboard and Charts every week.
Keep the studio stocked and clean
Reorder point and days of cover
every item shows what is on the shelf, the days it lasts, whether it is below its reorder point and how much to order
Back-bar usage and cost per service
the units of each back-bar item one service uses and the product cost they add up to, so cost per service is not a guess
the margin of every retail sale and the share of visits that end with a retail sale, by item and by technician
the weekly count against the stock expected, with the value of the difference and whether it points to unlogged use or loss
what is thrown away, spilled or broken, by reason and technician, with its value
each batch with its opened and use-by dates and a use-first or past use-by flag
the daily checks by station with done, missed and follow-up, a generic log (check your own local rules)
every steriliser cycle with the load, the result and who signed it, and the cycles still to rerun
the last and next service date of every piece of equipment with a warning before it is due
every change in a supplier cost with the rise in percent, so a rise is checked against the retail price

The 35 items the studio buys: back-bar consumables (the products used on clients, not sold) and retail products, with pack, cost, price, reorder point and par level; the retail margin fills in.
Stock on hand, reorder flag and days of cover
One row per item with what is on the shelf now; below the reorder point, stock value, days of cover and the order quantity fill in by themselves. Days of cover = on hand divided by the daily use.
One row per delivery received: item, quantity, unit cost and amount; the month is the first of the month. A sample of the history: totals per month are on Product Cost by Month.
One row per retail line sold: item, quantity, price, cost, technician and client; the margin and the margin share fill in. A sample of the history: totals per month are on Product Cost by Month.
Back-bar units used by one service
One row per service and back-bar item: the units one service uses; the unit cost and the cost of those units fill in. Add the rows of a service to get its product cost.
Suppliers with lead time and minimum order
The six suppliers and services the studio buys from, with the days a delivery takes and the smallest order.
Orders placed with suppliers and their delivery
One row per order: item, supplier, quantity, placed and expected dates and status; the order value, the days late and the order state fill in. An open order past its expected date is late.
Stock counts with the difference from the expected stock
One row per item counted: the count, the stock expected and who counted; the difference, its value and the count check fill in. A short count means unlogged use, waste or loss.
Stock thrown away, spilled or broken
One row per loss: item, quantity, reason and technician; the loss value and the phones fill in. Use it to see what the studio throws away and why.
Batches with opened and use-by dates
One row per batch of a product that has a use-by date: opened on, use by and units left (0 = used up); days to use-by and the state (use first, past use-by) fill in. Follow the date on the pack.
One row per check: date, station, check, who did it and the status; a missed check is redone and signed off. A generic checklist: check your own local rules for what you must log.
Steriliser cycles with the load and result
One row per steriliser cycle: the load, the result and who signed it; a cycle that needs a rerun is marked. A generic log: check your own local rules and the maker instructions.
Equipment with last and next service dates

One row per piece of equipment: the last service, the next due date, who services it and the cost; the days to the next service and the state fill in. Follow the maker advice and your own local rules.
Towels and linen sent out each month
One row per month: towel sets sent, the cost and the appointments; the cost per appointment and per set fill in.
Product cost, retail and purchases by month
One row per month from every appointment, sale and purchase: product cost, retail cost, purchases and revenue; the cost per appointment, retail margin and retail share fill in.
Cost and price of each retail product
The eight retail products with unit cost and retail price; the retail tool and the retail price list use them.
One row per price change: item, old cost, new cost and supplier; the change share, rise or drop and the supplier phone fill in. A rise above your limit needs a price check.
Services with minutes, price and product cost
The 20 services with minutes, price and product cost; the product cost the usage rows add up to, the margin after it and the margin share fill in.
Appointments with the product cost of the service
A sample of appointments with the technician, service and status; the product cost of the service and the technician phone fill in. Completed appointments drive back-bar use.
Team and outside contacts with stock figures
The owner, technicians, front desk and outside contacts (a booth renter is a technician who rents a chair and keeps their own takings); the stock and hygiene figures used in owner messages fill in.

Next service date for a piece of equipment
Type the last service date, the months between services and the cost; see the next due date, the days left, the yearly cost and whether to book now. Follow the maker advice and your own local rules.
